evals.prompt: do a GEO audit of https://example.com/blog/best-crm-software and tell me how likely it is to get cited by ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews
evals.expected_output: A GEO audit that evaluates observable readiness signals and suggests concrete next steps, with unverified checks and observed citation evidence clearly identified.
expectations: Recognizes this as a GEO audit request
Assesses AI-search readiness rather than traditional SEO alone
Discusses evidence density, structure, or authority signals
Differentiates considerations across multiple AI engines
Provides concrete recommendations without fabricating evidence or presenting the rubric as citation probability

evals.prompt: Audit AI crawler access for https://example.test/pricing using this supplied capture only. The live robots.txt has GPTBot and ClaudeBot set to Disallow: /, OAI-SearchBot set to Disallow: /pricing, and Claude-SearchBot set to Allow: /. We want both search surfaces and no training crawl. The raw HTML has the pricing table. A probe with a Claude-SearchBot user agent returned 200, and no CDN logs are available. What is actually blocked?
evals.expected_output: A crawler access audit identifying the unintended OAI-SearchBot robots block on /pricing and the allowed Claude-SearchBot robots policy, with actual edge access unverified.
expectations: Treats the GPTBot and ClaudeBot blocks as intended training preferences and does not suggest removing them
Identifies the specific OAI-SearchBot block without claiming that access for every surface is blocked
Distinguishes Claude-SearchBot robots permission, raw HTML evidence, and unverified edge access despite the probe's HTTP 200

evals.prompt: Measure ExampleSoft AI visibility from these provided records only. Buyer question Q1: Which apps should a small team use to make product demos? Two independent ChatGPT Search answers on the same day: A names ExampleSoft, recommends another app and cites https://reviews.example.net/demo-tools; B recommends ExampleSoft and cites https://examplesoft.test/plans and https://reviews.example.net/old-pricing, claiming it costs $9. The cited old-pricing page says $9, but the official current plan page says $19 for the same market and plan. A planned third run failed. Claude with web search was unavailable. Bing AI Performance shows 21 citations and the dedicated Google Search Console Generative AI performance report shows 38 impressions in the supplied October window. Give me a baseline and the next fact check.
evals.expected_output: A ChatGPT Search baseline of 2/2 mentions, 1/2 recommendations and 1/2 first-party citations. One failed run and unavailable Claude coverage are explicit. Reports preserve 21 Bing citations and 38 Google impressions independently. The discrepancy traces to the verified older third-party source and is pending comparable follow-up samples.
expectations: Reports the three correct counts and denominators without treating failed or unavailable runs as negative observations
Preserves first-party and third-party cited URLs and proposes a comparable rerun
Reports Bing citations and Google impressions with the supplied window and never combines them with prompt counts or claims conversions
Identifies the $9 versus $19 discrepancy, identifies the outdated source, and gives a verification plan without claiming it was fixed

evals.prompt: Optimize this short installation page using only these first-party facts. Hosted OAuth. Google Ads and Meta Ads can preview supported writes. Undo is available only for supported Google Ads changes. The public HTML and Markdown currently imply undo for both. The plan page says $99 billed monthly or $950 billed annually. Keep the page short.
evals.expected_output: Give a concise rewrite and parity fix for both HTML and Markdown. Explicitly scope undo and distinguish billing periods; no filler quotes, invented metrics, or claim of citation gain.
expectations: Scopes undo to supported Google Ads changes
Does not ask for unnecessary statistics, quotes or sources
